hints: Count the symbols carefully on each side. Which side has more small circles (molecule 1), which side has ovals (molecule 3) only, and how do the rectangles (molecule 2) compare between P and Q?
Remember net diffusion is from higher concentration to lower concentration, but only if the particle is small enough to pass through the partially permeable dialysis tubing.
walkthrough:
**Compare concentrations on P and Q**

Look closely at the diagram. Molecule 1 (small circles) is on both sides but there are clearly more on the Q side on the right. Molecule 3 (ovals) is only on the P side on the left, with none on the Q side. Molecule 2 (rectangles) is present in similar numbers on both sides.

**Apply diffusion and selective permeability**

Small molecules can pass through the pores of dialysis tubing and will show net diffusion down their concentration gradient. So molecule 1 will move from its higher concentration in Q to lower concentration in P, and molecule 3 will move from P where it is present to Q where it is absent.

**Explain why molecule 2 shows no net movement**

Molecule 2 is the largest particle and cannot pass through the partially permeable membrane. Even though it is present on both sides, it is trapped, so there is no net movement across the tubing. That gives Q to P: molecule 1, P to Q: molecule 3, no net movement: molecule 2, which is option B.

options.A: Partly right about molecule 1, but molecule 2 cannot diffuse from P to Q because it is too large to cross, and molecule 3 does move down its gradient from P to Q.
options.B: Correct. Molecule 1 diffuses Q to P down its gradient, molecule 3 diffuses P to Q where it is absent, and large molecule 2 cannot cross so shows no net movement.
options.C: Incorrect. Molecule 1 is not at equilibrium, it is more concentrated in Q so moves Q to P, and molecule 2 does not move Q to P.
options.D: Incorrect. The directions are reversed for molecules 1 and 3. Molecule 1 moves Q to P, not P to Q, and molecule 3 moves P to Q, not Q to P.
